correctness.rationale: For every outward rooted tree, the root-in-H case contributes u^N; root-outside-H and outside-W gives the child polynomial product; root-in-W requires exactly one child root outside H and gives v times the displayed sum. All cases partition the Wang pairs uniquely. Complete b-ary specialization gives C(0)=R(0)=2 and recurrences C_next=1+C^b+b(C-1), R_next=1+R^b. Logarithmic defects epsilon,delta are positive and tend to zero; the tail of the b-adic series is o(1) after multiplication by b^h. With C1=2^b+b+1 and R1=2^b+1, the positive explicit lower bound proves kappa_b>0. Independent finite direct semigroup congruence enumeration and a second bivariate polynomial checker both completed with VERIFY_OK; finite checks are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Wang (2018, Theorem 1.4) establishes the bijection between graph congruences and triples; in a DAG, this becomes (H,W). The new contribution is an explicit bivariate branching enumerator for all outward trees together with a strict positive entropy gap and exp(-kappa_b*b^h+o(1)) Rees probability. Inspected structural and lattice-property papers do not state or imply these quantitative formulas without the additional branching and asymptotic arguments. Literature priority is provisional, as broader unpublished enumeration could cover the result.
residual_risks: A nonlocated enumeration paper may explicitly supply the rooted-tree recursion or the free-energy limit.

value.rationale: Counting all congruences and distinguishing Rees congruences is an intrinsic semigroup-theoretic invariant, with structural relevance to ideal-generated quotients. For arbitrary finite out-trees the full two-variable distribution can now be generated locally. For an infinite natural family the strict, explicitly computable free-energy gap quantifies how rare the ideal-induced congruences become: exponentially in the graph vertex count. This is a motivated quantitative phenomenon rather than arbitrary table recomputation or merely the already known classification.
